query: Something to Stand Under Tobias kneels in an empty bed at the back of the greenhouse. "Ma used to say a farm's only as good as its shelter," he says, and presses his hands into the soil. A sapling comes up between you, then a trunk, then branches overhead. "Took me a year. I'll show you in an evening, if you like." Kneel down beside him You kneel in the cold soil until your knees ache and your back complains. Near midnight a little tree stands up out of your bed, wobbling, and spreads one branch over you. Tobias laughs from the belly and apologises for the mud. Sit under his tree instead You sit under his tree and he tells you a long story about a goat. It is very peaceful. "Another evening, then," he says, and means it.

Somewhere to Grow
The seed has outgrown your pocket. It needs a bed. Tobias offers the corner of his own in the greenhouse. Old Maud, passing, says there's a corner in her garden that never gets frost, "if you can keep a secret, dearie."

Storm Over the Greenhouses
A storm hits at midnight. Glass is cracking in the greenhouses. Tobias is out there in his nightshirt, trying to hold a door shut against the wind with his whole body. "The moonflowers!" he shouts. "Eleven years!"
